text:
maya: FYI — apse2 is seeing a sharp queue pileup for redwood-mosaic-4b. Queue depth jump: ~40 -> 280 in 12m. Tail latencies spiking, several 5xxs reported to clients. :rotating_light:
ian: paste the dashboard? link? :eyes:
maya: https://grafana.redwood/apse2/queue?range=15m — key metrics: admission_queue_len, per_model_pending[redwood-mosaic-4b], avg_token_latency.
ian: I see it. interestingly GPU utilization on the shard group is only ~45% but host CPU and network tx are high.
dinesh: that smells like KV cache churn or large prefix keys causing slow host-side prep. Can you paste the recent request-size histogram?
maya: request_size_hist snippet:
```
# Prometheus query
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_size_bytes_bucket{model="redwood-mosaic-4b"}[5m])) by (le))
```
95p jumped from 12kb -> 96kb in last 10m.
eva: If it's request expansion, the runtime is probably spending time on IO and sub-batching. Immediate mitigations: 1) enable per-model rate cap to throttle noisy tenants; 2) enable fallback routing for redwood-mosaic-4b -> redwood-mosaic-4b-q4b for non-latency-critical routes; 3) open a reroute to us-west warm pool for new requests. Which is fastest?
sarah: Rate cap + fallback is quickest. Rerouting requires config push and SAFETY review.
maya: can we do an on-the-fly rate cap? command below to set soft-cap for model via admin-api:
```
POST /admin/limits
{"model":"redwood-mosaic-4b","limit_rps":60,"scope":"global"}
```
That should shed backlog slowly.
dinesh: I'll check autoscaler logs — might be suppressed by our admission controller because of fairshare thresholds. If autoscaler thinks slots are idle but admission rejects growth, that's a bug.
deploy-bot: [1729005000] deploy redwood-mosaic-4b v2.1 -> v2.2 completed to apse2. Rollout: 100% at 1729005000.
maya: ah — recent rollout might have changed model memory profile. v2.2 uses bigger KV layout. Could explain cache thrash.
capacity-bot: alert: apse2 spot eviction rate increased by 12% in last 30m, available GPU capacity down by 3 nodes.
frank: I can approve a temporary borrow of us-west spare capacity. But we need an explicit rollback plan if cross-region increases cost.
eva: plan proposal: 1) set soft rate cap (maya) 2) enable fallback to q4b (eva) 3) patch autoscaler config to ignore admission-rejection as a negative signal (dinesh) 4) open capacity-swap to us-west for 30m (frank) 5) postmortem if rollout=v2.2 is causal.
sarah: I'll own rollout rollback checklist and coord with release-engineering.
dinesh: digging into autoscaler logs now — will report back in 5.
maya: applying rate cap now. Will monitor.
(2m later) maya: rate cap applied, admission queue delta reduced from +240 to +90 in 6m. Not back to normal though.
dinesh: autoscaler flapping logs show admission controller rejected scale-up due to "fairshare: preserve_reserved_pools" config. Patching to relax threshold for 10m. Pushing config in 30s.
(3m later) dinesh: patched. Autoscaler kicked new pods, we got 6 more slots online. Queue depth trending down: 280 -> 110.
maya: reroute to us-west warm pool initiated (frank approved). ~18% of new traffic shifted. No client complaints yet.
eva: enabling model fallback for non-critical traffic. command: `feast route --model redwood-mosaic-4b --fallback redwood-mosaic-4b-q4b --scope noncritical`
(1m later) eva: fallback enabled. Effective latency for noncritical down from 2.1s -> 1.3s, overall backlog now ~45.
frank: cost note — cross-region relay will add egress. Keep it <= 30m unless backlog recurs.
maya: marking incident for postmortem. Assigning owners: dinesh (infra debug), sarah (release/rollback), eva (fallback/routing), frank (capacity decisions).
sarah: will schedule a 15m sync in 20m to decide rollback.
maya: thanks all. Will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
